{{Short description|Generalization of dominating sets using fractional weights}}

[[File:Fractional dominating set.svg|thumb|The sum of the weights of each vertex and its neighbors (its [[neighborhood (graph theory)|closed neighborhood]]) is at least 1. The assignment of weights is therefore a '''fractional dominating set'''. One may consider the sum of all weights of the graph across all fractional dominating sets; the smallest of these is the graph's '''fractional domination number'''. The graph shown has an optimal set shown, with a total sum of <math>7/3</math>.]]

In [[graph theory]], a '''fractional dominating set''' is a generalization of the [[dominating set]] concept that allows vertices to be assigned fractional weights between 0 and 1, rather than binary membership. This relaxation transforms the domination problem into a [[linear programming]] problem, often yielding more precise bounds and enabling polynomial-time computation.

== Definition ==

Let <math>G = (V, E)</math> be a graph. A '''fractional dominating function''' is a function <math>f: V \to [0, 1]</math> such that for every vertex <math>v \in V</math>, the sum of <math>f</math> over the [[Neighbourhood (graph theory)|closed neighborhood]] <math>N[v]</math> is at least 1:<ref name="haynes1998">{{cite book |last1=Haynes |first1=Teresa W. |last2=Hedetniemi |first2=Stephen T. |last3=Slater |first3=Peter J. |title=Fundamentals of Domination in Graphs |publisher=Marcel Dekker |year=1998 |isbn=9780429157769 |pages=261-262}}</ref><ref name="goddard2020">{{cite book |last1=Goddard |first1=Wayne |last2=Henning |first2=Michael A. |chapter=Fractional Dominating Parameters |title=Topics in Domination in Graphs |editor1-last=Haynes |editor1-first=Teresa W. |editor2-last=Hedetniemi |editor2-first=Stephen T. |editor3-last=Henning |editor3-first=Michael A. |publisher=Springer |year=2020 |isbn=978-3-030-51117-3 |pages=349-363 |doi=10.1007/978-3-030-51117-3_10}}</ref>

:<math>\sum_{u \in N[v]} f(u) \geq 1</math>

The '''fractional domination number''' <math>\gamma_f(G)</math> is the minimum total weight of a fractional dominating function:

:<math>\gamma_f(G) = \min\left\{\sum_{v \in V} f(v)\right\}</math>

== Properties ==

For any graph <math>G</math>, the fractional domination number satisfies:<ref name="haynes1998"/>

:<math>\gamma_f(G) \leq \gamma(G) \leq \Gamma(G) \leq \Gamma_f(G)</math>

where <math>\gamma(G)</math> is the [[domination number]], <math>\Gamma(G)</math> is the upper domination number, and <math>\Gamma_f(G)</math> is the upper fractional domination number.

The fractional domination number can be computed as the solution to a linear program by utilizing [[strong duality]].<ref name="goddard2020"/>

For any graph <math>G</math> with <math>n</math> vertices, minimum degree <math>\delta</math>, and maximum degree <math>\Delta</math>:<ref name="goddard2020"/>

:<math>\frac{n}{\Delta + 1} \leq \gamma_f(G) \leq \frac{n}{\delta + 1}</math>

For any graph <math>G</math>, the fractional ''edge'' domination number equals the domination number of the [[line graph]]:<ref name="Shanthi2023"/>
:<math>\gamma'_f(G) = \gamma(L(G))</math>

== Formulas for specific graph families ==

For a [[regular graph|{{mvar|k}}-regular graph]] with <math>n</math> vertices and <math>k \geq 1</math>:<ref name="haynes1998"/><ref name="arumugam2012">{{cite journal |last1=Arumugam |first1=S. |last2=Mathew |first2=Varughese |last3=Karuppasamy |first3=K. |title=Fractional distance domination in graphs |journal=Discussiones Mathematicae Graph Theory |year=2012 |volume=32 |issue=3 |pages=449-459 |doi=10.7151/dmgt.1609 |doi-access=free}}</ref>

:<math>\gamma_f(G) = \frac{n}{k+1}</math>

For the [[complete bipartite graph]] <math>K_{r,s}</math>:<ref name="goddard2020"/>

:<math>\gamma_f(K_{r,s}) = \frac{r(s-1) + s(r-1)}{rs - 1}</math>

For the [[cycle graph]] <math>C_n</math>:<ref name="Shanthi2023">{{cite journal |last1=Shanthi |first1=P. |last2=Amutha |first2=S. |last3=Anbazhagan |first3=N. |last4=Bragatheeswara Prabu |first4=S. |title=Effects on fractional domination in graphs |journal=Journal of Intelligent & Fuzzy Systems |year=2023 |volume=44 |issue=5 |pages=7855–7864 |doi=10.3233/JIFS-222999}}</ref>
:<math>\gamma_f(C_n) = \frac{n}{3}</math>

For the [[path graph]] <math>P_n</math>:<ref name="Shanthi2023"/>
:<math>\gamma_f(P_n) = \left\lceil \frac{n}{3} \right\rceil</math>

For the [[crown graph]] <math>H_{n,n}</math>:<ref name="Shanthi2023"/>
:<math>\gamma_f(H_{n,n}) = 2</math>

For the [[wheel graph]] <math>W_n</math> with <math>n > 3</math> vertices:<ref name="Shanthi2023"/>
:<math>\gamma_f(W_n) = 1</math>

Several graph classes have <math>\gamma_f(G) = \gamma(G)</math>:<ref name="goddard2020"/>

* [[Tree (graph theory)|Trees]]
* [[Block graph]]s (graphs where every block is complete)
* [[Strongly chordal graph]]s

For the [[strong product of graphs]] <math>G \boxtimes H</math>:<ref name="goddard2020"/>

:<math>\gamma_f(G \boxtimes H) = \gamma_f(G) \cdot \gamma_f(H)</math>

For the [[Cartesian product of graphs]] <math>G \square H</math> ([[Vizing's conjecture]], fractional version):<ref name="goddard2020"/>

:<math>\gamma_f(G \square H) \geq \gamma_f(G) \cdot \gamma_f(H)</math>

== Computational complexity ==

Since the fractional domination number can be formulated as a linear program, it can be computed in polynomial time, unlike the standard domination number which is [[NP-hard]] to compute.<ref name="goddard2020"/>

== Variants ==

A '''fractional distance k-dominating function''' generalizes the concept by requiring that for every vertex <math>v</math>, the sum over its distance-<math>k</math> neighborhood <math>N_k[v]</math> (vertices at distance at most <math>k</math> from <math>v</math>) is at least one. The corresponding '''fractional distance k-domination number''' is denoted <math>\gamma_{kf}(G)</math>. <ref name="arumugam2012"/>

For <math>k</math>-regular graphs and specific values of <math>k</math>, exact formulas exist. For instance, for cycles <math>C_n</math>:<ref name="arumugam2012"/>

:<math>\gamma_{kf}(C_n) = \frac{n}{2k+1}</math>

An '''efficient fractional dominating function''' satisfies

:<math>\sum_{u \in N[v]} f(u) = 1</math>

for all vertices <math>v</math>. Not all graphs admit efficient fractional dominating functions.<ref name="goddard2020"/>

A '''fractional total dominating function''' requires that for every vertex <math>v</math>, the sum over its open neighborhood <math>N(v)</math> (excluding <math>v</math> itself) is at least one. The '''fractional total domination number''' is denoted <math>\gamma_{ft}(G)</math>.<ref name="goddard2020"/>

The '''upper fractional domination number''' <math>\Gamma_f(G)</math> is the maximum weight among all minimal fractional dominating functions.<ref name="goddard2020"/>
